data.message: Retrieving the official financial statement PDF from the CSE document repository
Document secured and staged for processing
Running multi-dimensional financial health diagnostics with LLM (this may take a minute)...
Health diagnostics finalised for BALA.N0000 — overall score: 43/100 · Poor

standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Current ratio stands at 1.17x, but the quick ratio is significantly lower at 0.50x due to high inventory holdings (Rs. 452.8M). Short-term liquidity is heavily reliant on bank overdrafts, which expanded from Rs. 103.9M to Rs. 187.4M.

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Revenue declined by 15% YoY to Rs. 843.2M. The company suffered a gross loss of Rs. 117.7M (gross margin of -13.96%) and a net loss of Rs. 41.2M, down from a net profit of Rs. 132.2M in Q1 2025.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Long-term interest-bearing leverage relative to total equity (Rs. 4.64B) is moderate. However, interest coverage ratio drops below 1.0x (Operating Profit of Rs. 15.6M vs Finance Cost of Rs. 19.5M), creating short-term debt servicing pressure.

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Operating cash flows turned negative at Rs. (13.9M) compared to positive Rs. 74.7M in Q1 2025. Free cash flow is negative due to ongoing capital expenditures, widening net cash deficits to Rs. (143.0M).

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Segment Operational Margin Contribution
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Both primary operating segments suffered gross losses: Tea reported a segment loss of Rs. 109.4M (-16.0% gross margin) and Rubber reported a loss of Rs. 8.3M (-5.2% gross margin), revealing severe production cost inflation relative to market selling prices.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: In plantation companies, monitoring crop-level gross margins (Tea vs. Rubber) is crucial to evaluate core yield efficiency, labor cost control, and field-level profitability.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Biological Asset Earnings Reliance
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Consumable and bearer biological assets account for over 59% of total assets (Rs. 5.43B). Reported operating profit of Rs. 15.6M relied entirely on a Rs. 100.9M non-cash fair value gain on biological assets; without it, core operating results are deep in loss.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Plantation financial statements often rely on non-cash biological asset revaluations, making it critical to separate cash operating earnings from fair value accounting gains.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Reinvestment in Bearer Assets (Field Development)
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Capital expenditure on immature bearer biological assets was Rs. 9.2M in Q1 2026. Total CapEx of Rs. 32.0M remained below depreciation and amortization (Rs. 55.8M), suggesting potential under-investment in long-term field replanting.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Continuous replanting and field development in immature crops are vital for sustaining long-term agricultural yields and tree crop age profiles.

recommendations: Implement stringent cost-control measures in field operations and factory processing to reverse gross losses in both Tea and Rubber segments.
Optimize inventory management and reduce cash conversion cycle to improve the quick ratio and lower reliance on high-cost bank overdrafts.
Review tea and rubber selling price realizations and evaluate product mix diversification towards higher-margin specialities or value-added grades.
Restructure short-term bank borrowings to reduce net finance expenses, which currently exceed operating profits.
result.analysisNotes: Balangoda Plantations PLC experienced a challenging Q1 2026, marked by a 15% revenue decline and gross losses across both Tea and Rubber divisions. While total equity remains strong at Rs. 4.64B, operating profitability and cash flows have deteriorated, leaving the company dependent on non-cash biological asset revaluation gains to post positive operating profit.
